solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Set tough boundaries for election

parts.note: something tough is hard

indicators.note: the boundaries of a word are its outermost letters, so take the ends of election

explanation.surface: A call for strict rules governing how an election is run.
explanation.definitionFit: To set, as jelly or concrete sets, is to become firm and solid.

clue.text: Piece of garden equipment reportedly weeds earth around seed

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word is heard spoken, not written

parts.note: to weed a bed is to hoe it, so weeds gives hoes
a pip is a small fruit seed
E is the standard abbreviation for earth, as on plugs; around only places it beside the seed

explanation.surface: A gardener's tool described as one that weeds and spreads earth over seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weeds' as a verb is HOES, and 'reportedly' says it is heard: it sounds like HOSE. 'around' only loosely joins the earth to the seed; the earth simply follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A long flexible tube for watering is standard kit in a garden shed.

clue.text: Italian food recipe with mayonnaise coating the gravlax core

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions

indicators.note: coating means the sauce wraps round the next piece

parts.note: aioli is a garlic mayonnaise

indicators.note: the core of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: A fusion recipe in which garlic mayonnaise is smeared over cured Scandinavian salmon.
explanation.walkthrough: Gravlax has seven letters, so its core is the fourth, V.
explanation.definitionFit: Small stuffed pasta parcels are a classic dish from Italy.

clue.text: Weariness in endless hours of darkness on the Somme

parts.note: en is French for in, the French flavour set by the Somme

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.words: hours of darkness on the Somme
parts.note: the Somme is a French river, so the hours of darkness there are nuit, French for night

explanation.surface: A soldier's exhaustion through the long nights of the Somme battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the Somme' tells the solver to work in French: EN for in and NUIT for night, which 'endless' cuts to NUI.
explanation.definitionFit: A word borrowed from French for listless boredom and tiredness of spirit.

clue.text: Depth of resistance in Germany I initially never expected so soon

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
ich is German for I

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A report of German resistance proving deeper than anyone predicted so early.
explanation.definitionFit: Depth of colour or flavour is its fullness, a near synonym.

clue.text: International politician sacked EEC intern for disrespectful behaviour

parts.note: MP, member of parliament, is a politician

indicators.note: sacked suggests the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A politician fires a European Community intern for being rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' looks like the dismissal in the story but rearranges EEC and INTERN into ERTINENCE. The EEC was the European Economic Community.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheek or insolence towards others is a close synonym.

clue.text: Graduate student tucks into semikosher meal of fennel say

indicators.note: tucks into says the graduate and student go inside the other pieces

parts.note: semi asks for half of kosher, here its back half
tea is a light meal
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student tucking into a half-kosher dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semikosher' is one word made up for the surface: half of kosher, its last three letters. 'tucks into' puts the graduate and student between those letters and the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: An infusion made from fennel is one example of a herb-based drink; 'say' marks the example.

clue.text: Queen Elizabeth's initial inclination is against gold

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to lean is to incline, so a lean is an inclination
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A queen's personal preference running against gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious Queen Elizabeth is a red herring; the answer is a different queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor of Aquitaine was queen consort of both France and England.

clue.text: Singer said to be a monster

indicators.note: said to be signals the singer's name heard aloud

parts.note: Cilla Black was a British pop singer and TV presenter

explanation.surface: Someone calls a certain vocalist a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Cilla Black was a 1960s Liverpool singer, later a television host.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, the six-headed sea creature facing Charybdis across the strait.

clue.text: Learned to reverse vessel with a set of books

indicators.note: reverse turns the vessel's letters back to front

parts.note: vas is an anatomical duct or vessel
NT, the New Testament, is a set of biblical books

explanation.surface: Instructions learned for backing a boat up, with a library thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learned' reads as a past-tense verb but is the adjective, pronounced learn-ed.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholarly, erudite person is a savant; the word also works as an adjective for scholarly.

clue.text: Disputes really regularly with only a small number

parts.note: to spar is to argue, so spars means disputes

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter

explanation.surface: Arguments that genuinely happen in very small numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinly or scantily spread, meaning there are few of something.

clue.text: Journalist backs freedom of thought

indicators.note: backs means the journalist's letters are turned round

parts.note: ED, editor, is a journalist
liberation is freedom

explanation.surface: A reporter supports the right to think freely.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful consideration and weighing up of a matter is a form of thought.

clue.text: Free to rip off beneficiary of the black market

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are out of order

explanation.surface: A wartime spiv happy to cheat buyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rip off' seems a phrase, but 'rip' is fodder and 'off' alone rearranges FREE TO RIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes excessive gains from scarcity, typically by illicit trade.

clue.text: Cancel yearbook with one missing article

indicators.note: missing means the article is taken out

parts.note: an annual is a book published each year
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A yearbook is cancelled because one piece in it is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare void or invalid, as a court does to a marriage.

clue.text: Leading politicians first arranged sit in among pitmen

parts.note: prime means first, as in prime position

indicators.note: in among means the rearranged letters go inside the miners

parts.note: pitmen work down a pit, so they are miners

indicators.note: arranged rearranges the letters

explanation.surface: A sit-in staged by heads of government among coal miners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges the three letters of sit, and 'in among' places the result inside the pitmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Heads of government lead their cabinets and are the foremost politicians.

clue.text: He bills me to repair and decorate

indicators.note: to repair hints that the letters are broken and put back together differently

explanation.surface: A tradesman charges me for repairs and redecoration.
explanation.definitionFit: To adorn or add ornamental detail to something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: You and I will support unknown vicar to turn up OK

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath
to turn up in a down clue means reading upwards, so the letters reverse

parts.note: y is an algebraic unknown
Rev, Reverend, is a vicar's title
we'll is the contraction of we will, you and I will

explanation.surface: A couple promise to back a mysterious clergyman if he shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in WE'LL is ignored, giving WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying fine or all right as an agreement is the same as OK.

clue.text: Can't not say no after a large drink

indicators.note: after puts the refusal behind the drink

parts.note: a double is a large measure of spirits
a negative is a way of saying no

explanation.surface: Someone unable to refuse once a big drink is in front of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Two negatives in one phrase cancel out; this phrase is an example.

clue.text: Best sports centre is in the open air

parts.note: to best someone is to outdo them

indicators.note: the centre of a six-letter word is its middle two letters

explanation.surface: The top sports facility is an open-air one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective but is the verb meaning beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing something done or located outside rather than under a roof.

clue.text: Is love dead? Divorce!

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
the late person is a dead one

explanation.surface: A spouse decides the romance is over and demands a split.
explanation.definitionFit: Divorce as a verb means to separate or cut off, as does the answer.

clue.text: Leading saint's extremely approachable

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint

indicators.note: extremely keeps only the extremities of the word, its outer pairs of letters

explanation.surface: A prominent saint described as very easy to talk to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' keeps the two letters at each end of APPROACHABLE: AP and LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple food or product is the main or chief one, hence foremost.

clue.text: Complete wreck

definitions.meaning: complete as in absolute or utter
to wreck a car beyond repair, as in writing it off

explanation.definitionFit: Utter or absolute, and also a verb for demolishing a vehicle completely.

clue.text: Additional entrance at the back of the conservatory

parts.note: access is a way in

indicators.note: at the back of keeps only the closing letters of the word, dropping the rest

explanation.surface: A further door fitted at the rear of a glass extension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the back of' keeps just the last three letters of conservatory, ORY.
explanation.definitionFit: An accessory is something extra or supplementary, used as an adjective.

clue.text: Part of a Chinese verb

indicators.note: of signals that the answer is made of letters from the next words

explanation.surface: A grammatical query about a piece of a Chinese verb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' looks like the hidden-word signal but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To part is to separate or cut apart, a synonym.

clue.text: Impose ban in support of strike over British independence

parts.note: pro means for, in support of

indicators.note: over means one piece covers the other, so the strike surrounds the abbreviations

parts.note: to hit is to strike

explanation.surface: Backing a walkout over British independence, then forbidding it.
explanation.definitionFit: To prohibit is to forbid officially, which is to place a ban on something.

clue.text: Adult woman swallowed fly

parts.note: A is the film classification for adult
Vi is a woman's name, short for Violet
to have swallowed food is to have ate it, past tense of eat

explanation.surface: An old woman who swallowed a fly, as in the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot an aircraft is to fly; the answer is a formal synonym.

clue.text: Doctors are no help without introduction of latest hearing aid

indicators.note: doctors means tampers with, so the letters get rearranged
the introduction of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Physicians cannot assist without the newest audio device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' rearranges ARE NO HELP, and 'without' removes the L from 'introduction of latest'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small speaker placed in the ear helps the listener hear sound.

clue.text: A trial or possibly a plea bargain

parts.note: a plea bargain is a deal struck with prosecutors

explanation.surface: A defendant faces either a court case or a negotiated plea.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful, testing experience, the sense of trial as hardship.
